newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says gets Russian backing in row, trade deals.
newsitem.headline: Iran says gets Russian backing in row, trade deals.

text.p: Iran said on Tuesday it had reached several trade deals with Russia and that Moscow had told Tehran it supported Iran in a row with the European Union over a German verdict that Iranian leaders ordered political killings.

"Russian officials share Iran's views on the Mykonos trial and the Russian president and prime minister reiterated that the European Union is committing an error at this time," Parliament Speaker Ali Akbar Nateq-Nouri was quoted by Tehran radio as saying after returning home from an official visit to Russia.

EU member states, except Greece, have said they would recall their ambassadors from Iran after a German court ruled Tehran leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant. Iran, which has repeatedly denied the accusation, said it would reciprocate.

Nateq-Nouri, quoted by Iran's IRNA news agency, said the two countries signed memoranda of understanding on drilling for oil and gas and Russian participation in a project to develop Iran's large offshore South Pars gas field in the Gulf, but gave no further details.
He said other memoranda signed covered making Tupolev aircraft and underground train wagons in Iran and setting up plants to make integrated circuits, IRNA said.
Agreements were also reached on the sale to Iran of an unspecified number of Tupolev planes and for setting up a joint plant to make cars in Russia, he said in remarks reported by the radio.
Tehran had said before the visit that the two states were due to sign a deal to manufacture Tupolev Tu-334 aircraft in Iran.

Nateq-Nouri, tipped as a leading candidate in presidential elections in May, was warmly received in Russia where President Boris Yeltsin and his political opponents joined in courting Iran despite Tehran's diplomatic row with the EU.
Iran has good ties with Russia which has signed an $800 million deal to complete an Iranian nuclear plant despite opposition from the United States.
